g_policy.reason: The offer is an opt-in banner. Its copy states the reward (30 minutes with no sponsored stories), declining changes nothing, and 'if the ad fails' covers a game that is not ready or a play that is not confirmed.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes of hidden sponsored cards, a feature_time reward with no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an article-open counter reaching 3, which is an app event and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed, locked or capped. Declining leaves the feed, articles, saving and sharing as they are, with sponsored cards shown as usual.

g_brand_safety.reason: The banner is app chrome under the pill bar on s01, which is rated safe. It is not inside a conversation and not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: For a product_change, the new resource (an ad-light reading window) is tied to the observed core loop f01, reading a story from the feed to an article. The app charges for nothing, so the tie to the core loop is what carries this check.

c2_evidence.reason: The proposal claims AOL shows a full-screen video ad after every third article. The product model has no such ad and no AOL mention; s05 is only an in-article ad. This claim rests on something never observed.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid plan was observed, and the reward is a 30-minute window capped at 2 per day, so no subscription benefit is given away.

c5_moment.reason: The banner appears after the user finishes a third article and returns to the feed. It is a finished-action moment and does not interrupt reading.

c6_fits_simula.reason: This is a play-to-earn sponsored game. The reward is granted only once the play is confirmed, and the trigger is a detectable article-open counter.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the s01 feed slot below the first story, the s02 in-article Taboola card, and the article-to-feed reading loop, so it is specific to this app.

other_concern: Hiding Taboola or direct-sold native placements in exchange for a game may conflict with those partners' terms. Revenue displacement is also unmeasured, and the idea depends on the game earning more than the hidden cards.
